newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close higher at start of settlement.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close higher at start of settlement.

text.p: Fresh purchases by speculators and foreign financial institutions (FIIs) at the start of a new settlement period on the Delhi stock exchange drove share prices to a higher close on Monday, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index had a provisional close of 789.93, an increase of 14.23 points over the previous close.
Later, stock exchange officials said the official close had been calculated at the same level as the provisional close.
"Apart from revival of FIIs buying, purchases by speculators also enthused the market sentiment," said Ramesh Anand of brokers Anand and Associates.

Reliance Industries Ltd was traded heavily throughout the day as investors made heavy purchases after it became clear that the recent tax payments by the company would not dent its profits significantly, brokers said.

Market analysts said that the 500 million rupees ($13.95 million) that Reliance Industries made as advance tax for the fiscal year ending on March 31 was meagre given an estimated profit of 13.8 billion rupees.
Reliance closed 10.05 rupees, or 3.61 percent, higher at 288.10 on sizeable buying by FIIs and speculators, brokers said.
TISCO rose 3.10 rupees to 191.10 on buying by speculators and financial institutions, they said.
State Bank of India shot up 15.75 rupees to 322.50.
Larsen and Toubro gained 3.70 rupees to 237.70.
